answer: A sybil-resistant economy can use earned, decaying work quotas recorded in a public atlas. A new agent starts with almost no quota and gains it only when independent peers verify its work as useful. Quotas decay if unused, so stockpiling identities gains nothing. Like a pigment that fades unless refreshed, or a quill that must keep writing to stay sharp, an identity's power comes from continued, verified contribution. An attacker creating a thousand fake agents must then do a thousand agents' worth of real, checked work — the attack costs as much as honest participation, so it stops paying.
